identity.title: Open-World Reinforcement Learning over Long Short-Term Imagination

problem.claim: Improve exploration efficiency for visual reinforcement-learning agents making open-world decisions across vast state spaces, particularly when long-horizon payoffs matter.

gap.claim: Existing model-based agents are described as short-sighted because they are generally trained on short snippets of imagined experience.

contributions.claim: LS-Imagine extends the imagination horizon using a limited number of state-transition steps to explore behaviors that may yield promising long-term feedback.
The approach builds a long short-term world model using goal-conditioned jumpy state transitions and affordance maps derived by zooming into areas of single images.
The method integrates direct long-term values into behavior learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish LS-Imagine by extending imagination over a long short-term world model while retaining a limited number of state-transition steps.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant improvements over state-of-the-art techniques in MineDojo.

narrative_sequence.summary: Visual reinforcement learning in high-dimensional open worlds is difficult, with exploration spanning a vast state space and potentially long-horizon payoffs.
The abstract characterizes existing model-based agents as short-sighted because their imagined experiences are short.
LS-Imagine lengthens the imagination horizon within a limited transition budget, supported by a long short-term world model and image-based affordance maps.
The resulting mechanism incorporates direct long-term values into behavior learning.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art methods in MineDojo.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the exploration problem to long-horizon payoffs and describes a method that combines extended imagination with direct long-term values.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research framing can connect the decision-making difficulty, the mechanism, and the value signal in one causal-looking design rationale without claiming independent validation.
lessons.application: When presenting a planning method, explicitly map the target horizon problem to the planning-horizon mechanism and the value information it injects into learning.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the task objective is primarily short-horizon or when long-term value estimates are unavailable or unreliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify MineDojo tasks, baselines, metrics, improvement magnitudes, or evaluation conditions.
It does not provide quantitative evidence or details sufficient to assess how the limited transition budget compares with the effective imagination horizon.
